feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 5 (seven sensors at 20 mm spacing, +/-0.06 m span, 12 mm footprints, track 0.10 m) is the best measured result at 62.87. It removed line loss on the oval (0 events, progress 0.175) but left one line-loss event per run on the s-bend (progress 0.165) and slalom (progress 0.110), with max_error about 0.062 m. Iteration 6 showed the 16 mm footprint did not help in aggregate (62.13), so sensing is not the binding constraint. Iterations 0 to 3 showed the 0.06 m off-track floor is fixed, and drivetrain changes moved the score by about 0.14 in total. Depending on the next race: if line_loss_events fall toward 0 on the s-bend and slalom and max_error drops below 0.06 m, keep wheel_track 0.08 m and move to wheel_radius for ground speed. If max_error still sits near 0.06 m with line loss at 1, the yaw gain is not enough, so try wheel_track 0.09 m for a middle compromise. If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.17 (iteration 5 slalom was 0.152), the narrower track has overshot, so return to 0.09 m.
requested_changes: If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.17 with wheel_track 0.08 m (iteration 5 slalom was 0.152 at 0.10 m), try wheel_track 0.09 m as the compromise, citing the iteration 5 oscillation data.

If line_loss_events and max_error stay at 1 and about 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, the yaw authority change alone is not enough. Try wheel_radius 0.035 m for more ground speed, citing iterations 1 to 5, where lead, span, footprint and track changes all left oval progress at 0.16 to 0.175.
Keep sensor_size at 0.012 m and do not revisit the 16 mm footprint, since iteration 6 scored lower (62.13) than iteration 5 (62.87).
